node.label: Pierre Bourdieu
node.date_label: Esquisse d’une théorie de la pratique (1972) · Outline of a Theory of Practice, translated by Richard Nice (1977) · La Distinction (1979) · Distinction, translated by Richard Nice (1984) · “L’illusion biographique” (1986)
node.description: Develops a relational account of social practice, taste and narrated lives. His habitus connects acquired dispositions with improvisation rather than reducing conduct to explicit rules or unconstrained choice. The selected Distinction conclusion examines classificatory struggles and social position; it does not certify one universal mechanism for all tastes. In “L’illusion biographique” he challenges retrospective stories that present a life as a naturally continuous project. Trajectories must be reconstructed across changing social fields, including the institutions and interview situations that help produce a named person’s apparent unity. The entry reuses precisely bounded earlier primary readings rather than claiming a new reading of the complete books.
